messages:
leo: FYI saw a tail spike during a regional preemptive drain. root cause looks like proxy allowed fallback to us-east even though tenant has residency:EU-only. :grimacing:
maya: do we have a trace? was it a hard error or long retries?
leo: mostly long retries + occasional 409 from downstream consent check. logs show: `routing: selected region us-east-1 for tenant t-908 -> backend rejected write consent=deny -> proxy retried -> p99 rose`.
tom: i thought we cached tenant residency in the proxy? why did it try us-east?
leo: cache miss combined with fallback policy that selects next-closest region regardless of consent. cache TTL is 30s; during the drain there were simultaneous cache evictions and control-plane lag.
maya: control-plane lag is a separate reliability problem but proxy must not make cross-region decisions that violate residency. we need a safety check: if residency metadata missing, default to "deny cross-region write".
tom: agree. options: (1) change proxy default to deny when cache miss (2) make proxy synchronously fetch cp on miss (3) add a lightweight signed residency token in requests that always travels with tenant traffic. tradeoffs: (1) safest and fastest to ship, but may cause more local failures under CP flapping; (2) adds latency on miss; (3) long-term and more work but avoids cp roundtrips daily.
anya: legal: default deny on miss is mandatory for PII. any async fetch or token must have auditable issuance and TTL. also need retention of residency change events for compliance.
leo: proposal for immediate fix: set proxy config `residency_on_cache_miss = deny` and emit metric residency.cache_miss_blocked_total. fast rollbackable flag.
maya: add alerts: fire if residency.cache_miss_blocked_total > 5/min for any region so ops can intervene. also emit per-tenant blocked_count.
tom: mid-term plan: implement signed residency tokens issued by CP with 5m TTL. proxy validates signature locally and trusts token — no CP hit on normal path. token shape idea: `tenant_id|consent|allowed_regions|exp|sig` (base64). CP issues on change and on demand.
anya: legal happy with token approach if signature algo and audit logs are documented. need to show how revocations are handled (revoke list TTL or short token lifetime).
leo: long-term: move residency decisions earlier into the client SDK so that clients can prefer local-only writes when consent != allowed. but that's a product change.
maya: runbook changes: when planning a regional drain, operators should: 1) run residency preflight to ensure cache warmed and tokens provisioned for tenants with allowed fallback; 2) tag tenants without fallback as "pinned" so we don't try to move them; 3) schedule drains with shard-level slow-window (15-60m) and watch residency.blocked metric.
tom: i'll add proxy flag and the canary rollout. deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: proxy toggle residency_on_cache_miss=deny -> eu-canary 2024-06-03T14:00Z rollout 10%->50%->100%. :rocket:
leo: i'll write the small CP script to bulk-issue tokens for high-QPS tenants and set default pinned metadata for low-consent tenants.
anya: legal: add me to the RFC and include the revocation pattern + audit event examples (json payloads). also require default-privacy-mode note in the public docs.
maya: metrics list: residency.cache_miss_total, residency.cache_miss_blocked_total, residency.fallback_attempts_total{from,to}, residency.token_validation_failures_total. alerts for blocked per-tenant >5/min and token failures >1% of requests.
tom: follow-ups: (A) immediate prod flag (B) canary + metrics (C) token RFC with schema + revocation + CP tooling (D) client SDK note for long-term. i'll own A and C, leo owns B data prep, maya owns alerts, anya legal review.
leo: ok opening a short RFC + runbook fragment and will attach logs and sample audit events.
leo: thanks. sync tomorrow 11:00am PT to confirm canary health.
